title: Mayar and Driesh from Glenshee
listingBlurb: Two Munros off the ski centre — big ridges, obvious shape, not a puzzle day.
summary: Proper two-Munro round from Glenshee: up onto open ground, out along the broad ridge to Mayar and Driesh, then back. Simple enough in clear weather. No line on this page — no polyline, no GPX. The map’s just centred near the car park so you’ve got context.
suggestedRouteBadge: Hill day (no drawn line on this site)
parkingNote: Glenshee ski centre car park — watch seasonal charges, ski-day chaos, and where you’re actually allowed to leave the motor. Park like a normal human: don’t block gates or turn it into a rally stage. From there you’re into open hill; there’s no traced route on this site.

disclaimerSection.title: No line on this page
disclaimerSection.body: We’re not publishing a polyline, GPX, or waypoint list for this day. You still get parker, rough shape of the day, terrain, and how it usually feels — where you actually walk is your map and what it looks like on the ground.
disclaimerSection.supporting: Bring a map and use your brain. Check a mountain forecast. Don’t treat this page as a substitute for either.

weatherNote.title: Before you go
weatherNote.body: Mountain forecast for the bit of hill you’re on, not just the nearest town. Wind on these ridges can be a pain even when the glen looks fine.
weatherNote.supporting: Static blurb on a website, not a live readout.
weatherNote.disclaimerLabel: Always verify conditions on the day.

whyThisRoute.title: Why pick this day?
whyThisRoute.body: Decent shout if the weather’s rough or you don’t fancy a nav exam. You get height, air, and a ridge that mostly makes sense — less ‘where the hell’s the line?’ than some of the other Glen Esk days.
callouts: Clear two-Munro shape; ridge logic is usually obvious.
Often fine when you want big hill without inventing a new hobby.
whyThisRoute.supporting: Still a full day if the weather’s being a bastard — tired legs, wind, clag. Nav just tends to be kinder than the fiddly link-ups.

recommendationBlock.title: Rough take
lines: One of the easier days in the glen to hold in your head — big open ground, not much mystery in decent visibility.
Save the clever linking for another time unless you actually want more map work.
recommendationBlock.supporting: Late starts work here more often than on tight-window days — within reason. Don’t ignore sunset or winter daylight.

qualityMeter.headline: Solid day out with a readable shape
qualityMeter.verdict: Big and open; nav’s usually straightforward. Still a proper hill day, not a stroll.

factors.label: Ridge clarity
factors.note: The day usually sorts itself into a simple arc before you’ve left the car park.

factors.label: Weather exposure
factors.note: Open slopes and ridges — wind and clag can turn an easy day into a slog.

factors.label: Ski-centre start
factors.note: Busy and a bit utilitarian, but the start’s obvious for most folk.

factors.label: No traced line on this page
factors.note: We’re not drawing your line for you — bring map skills.

whatDayFeelsLike.title: What it feels like
whatDayFeelsLike.body: Big sky, proper hill underfoot, mostly straightforward ground. You find a pace, eat somewhere out of the wind if you’re lucky, and you’ve still earned your tea.
whatDayFeelsLike.supporting: Rough weather and clag can make it feel serious fast — it’s wind and tiredness, not circus tricks. Worth knowing how you’d shorten the day before you need to.
summaryLines: Headspace for chat or silence — your call.

terrainDetail.title: Terrain & vibe
terrainDetail.body: Grassy and heathery slopes opening onto cleaner ridge walking. Normal Scottish hill: some wet bits, some draggy bits, some genuinely nice bits if the light’s on your side.
terrainDetail.supporting: Winter changes the game — ice, windslab, short days; same rules as everywhere else.

goodStopsDetail.intro: Spots that often work for a break — not waypoints, just what usually helps.

spots.title: Somewhere out of the worst wind
spots.description: On the ridge, a slight dip or lee side beats lunch on the highest lump.

spots.title: Before anything committing
spots.description: If the clag comes down, slow up and check the map there — not after you’ve already committed to a vague downhill guess.

anchorRefsIntro: Labels for nattering and map-checking — not an order to follow.
notes: Good for: rough-but-readable weather, sensible late starts, straightforward ridge nav when you can see — not for zero-visibility heroics.
Ski-centre ops, events, and parking rules change — read what’s posted on the day.
Busy pair in good weather; early or late if crowds wind you up.
‘Drive to the parker’ uses the map centre near the ski centre — eyeball it against your own map before you drive.
planningFooterNote: From the Glen Esk area guide. Planning copy only — your line, your timing, your call.
